name: IEC summing amplifier element (Σ)
summary: Analogue element with Σ and several inputs, producing an output proportional to the weighted sum of the inputs.
description: A summing amplifier adds several analogue inputs, each with its own weighting. In IEC-style analogue element diagrams it is drawn as a rectangle with an amplifier mark and the Σ function, with weighting factors written next to each input. The usual circuit realisation is an inverting op-amp with one input resistor per signal.

Summers appear in control loops for combining set-point and feedforward signals, in audio-style mixing of measurements, and in analogue computation. The weighting factors and the sign of the output must be stated because an inverting realisation reverses polarity.
The element does not show the resistor network that sets the weights. For a construction schematic, the op-amp circuit with values should be drawn or referenced.
readingNotes: Weighting factors are written beside the inputs.
An inverting realisation gives a negative sum unless followed by an inverter.
distinction: The digital Σ adder adds binary words; the analogue summing element adds voltages or currents.
